data.content_ref: inline:exp-hist:{"target": "5ba7a0652869a36673791dc2f6fff77a7a20626eb0d4d0034c8ffe46ddd9754b", "seq": 1, "objection": "The target's defense fails to address the 'smuggling induction' charge because its reliance on 'survival' as a marker for being the 'most informative error-eliminated option' implicitly assumes that past survival is a reliable indicator of future robustness or utility. Popper explicitly rejected the idea that surviving tests makes a theory more probable or reliable for the future; by arguing we should prefer the survivor *because* it has survived, the target reinstates an inductive principle (that the future will resemble the past regarding test outcomes) which Popper deemed irrational. The target claims this is merely a 'strategic move,' but without an inductive bridge, there is no Popperian justification for why the 'error-eliminated' status of the past theory should guide action in the present any more than a random guess would, rendering the preference indefensible on strictly non-inductive terms.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
